message.content:
In the 19th‑century canon, **Auguste Rodin’s “The Kiss” (1889)** is often cited as the single most iconic sculpture of that era.  It captured the Romantic fascination with intimate, expressive form and became a worldwide symbol of love and passion.

Other works that rival its fame include:

| Sculpture | Artist | Year | Why it matters |
|-----------|--------|------|----------------|
| **“The Gates of Hell”** | Rodin | 1880–1917 | A monumental, mythologically charged work that influenced modern sculpture. |
| **“The Burghers of Calais”** | Rodin | 1889 | A powerful civic monument reflecting the social concerns of the time. |
| **Statue of Liberty** | Frédéric Bartholdi | 1886 | A national symbol that also showcases 19th‑century engineering and artistic skill. |

So while there isn’t a single definitive “most famous” sculpture, Rodin’s “The Kiss” stands out as the quintessential 19th‑century masterpiece.
